summary:
THE FORGOTTEN WITNESSES – ASTRAFORGE

ASTRAFORGE developed The Forgotten Witnesses, an illustrated visual story exploring the objects humanity has left behind during space exploration. From Apollo landing equipment and footprints on the Moon to abandoned Mars rovers, scientific instruments and deep-space spacecraft. This project uncovers the stories behind these often-overlooked witnesses of human discovery.

Through research, storytelling and visual documentation, we explore what happens to space equipment when missions end, why some objects continue serving scientific purposes and how others become historical evidence of humanity's journey beyond Earth.

Our project addresses the challenge by highlighting the forgotten side of space exploration: not just the destinations we reach, but the traces we leave behind. This is important because these objects represent scientific achievements, engineering innovation and humanity's responsibility to protect the environments we explore.

Their missions ended, but their stories remain.
details:
PROJECT DETAILS – THE FORGOTTEN WITNESSES

ASTRAFORGE developed The Forgotten Witnesses, an illustrated digital storytelling project that explores the objects humanity has left behind during space exploration.

The project works by combining scientific research, informative storytelling and visual illustrations to document forgotten space exploration equipment across the Moon, Mars and deep space. It takes readers through the history, purpose and significance of these objects by explaining what happened to them after their original missions ended.

We used NASA's publicly available research and educational resources to guide our content, alongside written narration, digital document design and SI to help readers visualise the environments and objects being discussed.

The project's creativity lies in presenting space exploration from a different perspective rather than focusing only on astronauts, rockets and discoveries. We tell the stories of the machines and equipment that made exploration possible even though they were left behind.

In addition, our team considered scientific accuracy, historical significance, visual presentation, readability and most importantly to educate and inspire readers, as well as encourage responsible space exploration and highlight the importance of preserving evidence of humanity's journey beyond Earth.

Ultimately, we want readers to understand that space exploration is not only about where humanity goes, but also about what humanity leaves behind and why?
